qualification_limits: The console's 20 functional observations passed; the original overall harness status remains FAIL because the Chrome job reached its 128-task cap 11 times. The SCHISM server and driver had zero task-cap events. This resource exception remains recorded.
Native artifacts are qualified on Windows 11 AMD64 and Linux x86_64/glibc 2.43. Other operating systems, architectures and older Linux C libraries require their own validation.
Source dependency metadata accepts Python 3.11 or newer. Actual source execution was exercised on Python 3.12.14, 3.13.15 and 3.14.4 in the recorded environments.
The standalone controller embeds its runtime. Applications retain their own executable/runtime prerequisites; {python} in a native distribution requires an external Python.
Applications execute with the operator's OS-account authority. Isolation from hostile publisher code requires a separately enforced OS/container/VM boundary.
Service updates restart the service and can cause downtime. Recovery attempts the previous authorized code; failed restart remains a visible outcome.
Code rollback retains current data. Candidate writes, external effects, application migrations and exactly-once transactions require application-specific contracts.
Detached work outlived individual CLI and SSH callers in the recorded environments. Qualification did not remove outer host-job containment or establish reboot persistence.
Signed evidence establishes content, key and recorded-event consistency. Compromised signing hosts, physical hardware identity and external factual truth remain separate trust boundaries.
The SSH command adapter targets POSIX recipients using existing account authentication and strict host-key checking. It does not configure remote accounts or install remote software.

ssh_qualification.authority: Existing operator-owned SSH authentication with pinned host key and retained recipient public key
limits: The qualified remote recipient uses a POSIX SSH shell.
